newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain's 156 year rule in HK will end in 35 minutes.
newsitem.headline: Britain's 156 year rule in HK will end in 35 minutes.

text.p: More than 150 years of British colonial rule will end in a 35-minute ceremony, a Hong Kong official coordinating the territory's handover to China said on Monday.
Britain raised its flag in Hong Kong in 1841 and is returning the territory to China at midnight on June 30.

Stephan Lam of the Handover Ceremony Coordination Office told legislators the sovereignty transfer would take slightly more than half an hour, including a guard of honour salute, the lowering of the British Union Jack and the raising of China's red flag.
"There will be a formal salute of military honour guards," Lam told a select committee on the handover ceremonies. Senior representatives of the two governments will then give speeches.
"The British national anthem will be played as the United Kingdom and Hong Kong flags are being lowered. Then the Chinese national anthem will be played," he said.
Lam said Britain and China had invited representatives from more than 40 countries.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is so far the most senior VIP guest of China and Britain to confirm she will attend, invited by both sides.
